lives_at.note: Not attested: the lists that name this person give no address. The placement sweep assigns homes once the resident list is complete (T-0514, the owner's own sequencing) and this pass will not guess one.

works_at.note: Not attested. No trade is recorded here, so there is no premises to seek; T-0633 is where a later directory's address gets back-projected.

present_on_scene_date.note: THE RECORD DOES NOT REACH THE DAY. Every source that names this person falls on one side of 1 July 1835, and nothing follows them to it or says they left. `uncertain` rather than dropped — the distinction index.json draws for Jeremiah Porter, and a finding, not a gap.

THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 1 time, as “BARRY JOHN R”, 1835-06-26: 1 federal land entry — W2SW sec 20 T39N R13E, 80.00 acres stated in all, for $100.00 (ls0813). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: BARRY JOHN R matches J R Barry: the forename names J R Barry of the 3 people of this surname, and the forename agrees as an initial only. (data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a land entry is a second source about a TRANSACTION rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835 — a man may buy a quarter-section he never sees. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict. THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 1 time: Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 — “Barry, J. R.” (poll_1834_007, line 176). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Barry' agrees with the entry's forenames; 3 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json).

merge_ruling.for_merge: One letter of surname and the forename initial J on both, and the town's only other Barry readings are these three cards.
merge_ruling.against_merge: R AND S ARE BOTH PRINTED AND THEY DISAGREE. 'John S. Barre' is the post-office return of 9 July 1834 (#c003); 'Barry, J. R.' is the poll filed 11 August 1834. Neither card is documented beyond a list — no trade, no address, no arrival — so C4's anchor is missing and the contradiction has nothing to be weighed against. This is exactly the `barry-j` cluster's ruling, which refuses J. R. against John S. within the Barry spelling; folding the surname as well cannot rescue it. R3.

merge_ruling.for_merge: `Barry, J. R.` of the 1834 poll list and `John S. Barry` of the letter list of 20 May 1835 share the surname and the forename initial, and the town holds no third Barry.
merge_ruling.against_merge: R and S are both printed and they disagree. Neither card is documented beyond a list — a poll roll and a letter list, no trade, no address, no arrival — so C4's anchor is missing and the contradiction has nothing to be weighed against. R3.
